key_insight: A multimodal deep learning model can combine CT anatomy and routine clinical data to automatically classify pancreatic cancer resectability into NCCN categories.
clinical_relevance: If validated, this could support more consistent treatment planning by reducing variability in expert judgment of vessel involvement on CT.
method: 3D contrast-enhanced CT analyzed with a Swin-UNETR backbone
Auxiliary segmentation of pancreas, tumor, and vascular structures to learn anatomy-aware features
Fusion of image features with 17 clinical variables and a lightweight classification head using a dynamic multitask loss
evidence_signal: The abstract describes a fully automated framework evaluated for three-class NCCN resectability classification, but it does not report performance metrics or cohort size.
watch_item: Clinical deployment would depend on external validation and robustness across scanners, institutions, and varied CT quality.
paper_title: Multimodal Assessment of Pancreatic Cancer Resectability Using Deep Learning
